instructions: Downtime Log & Pareto
Version 1.0
What this does
Record every stop with a reason. The Pareto sheet ranks reasons by minutes lost so you can see the few causes behind most of your downtime, for any date range and any machine.
Colour key
Yellow cells are for you to fill in.
Grey cells are calculated. Don't type over them.
Steps
1. Setup: list your machines, and edit the reason list to match how your plant talks about stops. Each reason has a category (Breakdown, Material, and so on) that you can also rename.
2. Downtime Log: one row per stop. Enter start and end times, or type the minutes directly if you only know the duration. Stops that cross midnight are handled automatically.
3. Pareto: choose a date range and, optionally, one machine. Reasons are ranked automatically, with the cumulative percentage and a chart.
4. By Machine: total downtime and stop counts per machine for the same date range.
5. The rows marked EXAMPLE show the expected format. Before you start, select their yellow cells and press Delete. Don't delete whole rows.
Tips
Keep the reason list short (10-15 reasons). If 'Other' becomes one of your top reasons, read its notes and add the missing reason.

Pick reasons from the drop-down so spelling stays consistent. A typed reason that isn't on the Setup list shows 'Not in Setup'; its minutes are counted as Unclassified on the Pareto sheet until you fix it.
The Check column on the log should say OK. A stop counts when its duration is more than 0 minutes. Rows without a date, or with minutes that aren't a number of 0 or more, are left out of the totals.

instructions: OEE Tracker
Version 1.0
What this does
Log each shift's production per machine. The workbook calculates Availability, Performance, Quality and OEE for every shift and summarizes them by machine on the Dashboard, for any date range.
Colour key
Yellow cells are for you to fill in.
Grey cells are calculated. Don't type over them.
Steps
1. Setup: list your machines and each one's ideal cycle time (the fastest sustainable time to make one part, in seconds). For a line, use the time per finished unit at rated speed.

2. Production Log: add one row per machine per shift. Planned stops are scheduled time the machine is not expected to run (breaks, planned meetings). Unplanned downtime is everything else it was stopped.
3. Dashboard: optionally enter a From and To date. Leave them blank to include everything.
4. The rows marked EXAMPLE show the expected format. Before you start, select their yellow cells and press Delete. Don't delete whole rows.
How OEE is calculated
Planned production time = shift length - planned stops.   Run time = planned production time - unplanned downtime.
Availability = run time / planned production time.
Performance = (ideal cycle time x total parts) / run time.
Quality = good parts / total parts.   OEE = Availability x Performance x Quality.

Dashboard OEE = total ideal time for good parts / total planned production time. Times and counts are summed first, so long and short shifts, and machines with different cycle times, are weighted correctly.
Check column

The Check column on the log flags common entry mistakes: a machine missing from Setup, rejects higher than total parts, downtime longer than planned time, missing or non-number entries. Rows with an error are left out of the Dashboard. 'Check: performance above 100%' is a warning only (usually a cycle time that is too slow in Setup, or a miscounted total); that row still counts.
Target
85% OEE is a commonly cited 'world-class' benchmark. Set your own target on the Dashboard; many plants start well below that, and improvement against your own baseline matters more.

Version 1.0
What this does
List every recurring maintenance task with how often it's due. Log completions as they happen, and the plan shows each task's next due date and whether it is overdue, due soon or OK.
Colour key
Yellow cells are for you to fill in.
Grey cells are calculated. Don't type over them.
Steps

1. PM Plan: one row per asset + task, with the frequency in days (7 = every week, 30 = about monthly, 90 = about quarterly, 365 = about yearly). Due dates count fixed days from the last completion. If you know when a task was last done before you started using this workbook, enter it under 'Last done before log'.

2. Completion Log: each time a task is done, add a row with the date, the asset and the task, picked from the drop-downs so they match the plan exactly. The 'Matches plan?' column warns you if they don't.
3. The plan updates automatically: last completed date, next due date, days left and status.
4. Change the 'Due soon' window at the top of the PM Plan (default 7 days).
5. A task with no completion and no earlier date shows as due today, every day, until you log it or enter a last-done date.
Status 'Check frequency', 'Duplicate row' or 'Fill in asset and task' means that row needs fixing; the Needs fixing count is at the top.
6. The rows marked EXAMPLE show the expected format. Before you start, select their yellow cells and press Delete. Don't delete whole rows.
Tip
Sort or filter the PM Plan by Status to get this week's work list. Excel: Data > Filter.

formula: OR(I5="Check frequency",I5="Duplicate row",I5="Fill in asset and task")
